A geo system would be amazing. I hear they are extremely efficient and I understand the concept but I know next to nothing about how they actually work.

Geo systems basically move air through pipes/tubes under ground where the temperature is constant year round. That air is then used to cool or heat the structure. So this system uses a fraction of the energy that heaters and AC use.

Some of the larger higher end units use liquid instead of air but that's a much more complicated system for larger buildings.

California is actually offering tax credits trying to get people to install geo systems instead of AC because of the strain on their power grid. Geo systems also cost a fair amount more depending on the size of the house/building and the install.

A relative of mine who has a lake house was talking about checking into the cost of having it done and whether or not they could (would be permitted) to do this using the water/lake.

I think he did say it was pretty high to have one installed but he seemed really impressed with the results. He was suggesting that we look into it as well but if he was taken back by the expense I know that we wouldn't be able to afford it!

Still, from what little I do know about it, it seems fairly impressive, to me anyway.
